whatIsNostr.title: Nostr Explained Simply
whatIsNostr.description: Understand Nostr in 5 minutes. Learn how decentralized social media works, why it matters, and how it's different from traditional platforms.

questions.title: Protocol Name
questions.prompt: What does NOSTR stand for?

options.label: Notes and Other Stuff Transmitted by Relays

questions.explanation: NOSTR stands for 'Notes and Other Stuff Transmitted by Relays' - a simple, open protocol for decentralized social media.

questions.title: Decentralization
questions.prompt: What makes Nostr decentralized?

options.label: Anyone can run a relay, and users control their own keys
It's owned by a non-profit foundation

questions.explanation: Nostr is decentralized because anyone can run a relay server, and users own their cryptographic keys. There's no central authority or company controlling the network.

questions.title: Censorship Resistance
questions.prompt: How does Nostr resist censorship?

options.label: By using AI to detect banned content
By spreading data across many relays that anyone can run
By requiring government approval for relays

questions.explanation: Censorship resistance comes from distributing content across many independently-run relays. If one relay blocks you, others can still carry your content.

questions.title: Identity System
questions.prompt: What's the main difference between Nostr and Twitter/Facebook accounts?

options.label: Nostr uses cryptographic keys instead of email/password

questions.explanation: Nostr uses public/private key pairs for identity. Your public key (npub) is your identity, and your private key (nsec) proves you own it. No email, phone number, or central database required.

questions.title: Relay Function
questions.prompt: What do relays do in the Nostr network?

options.label: They store and forward messages between users

questions.explanation: Relays are servers that store your posts and make them available to other users. They forward messages but don't control who can post or what content is allowed.

questions.title: Nostr vs Fediverse
questions.prompt: How does Nostr differ from Mastodon and the Fediverse?

options.label: Nostr doesn't require choosing a server/instance to join
Nostr is owned by Elon Musk

questions.explanation: Unlike Mastodon where you must join a specific server/instance, Nostr users can use any relay without creating an account there. Your identity works everywhere instantly.

keysAndSecurity.title: Keys & Security
keysAndSecurity.description: Learn how to generate, save, and protect your Nostr keys. The complete security guide for beginners.

questions.title: Key Safety
questions.prompt: Which item can you safely share with anyone?

options.label: Your npub (public key)
options.description: Lets others follow or message you

questions.explanation: npub keys are public identity. Anything that starts with nsec or a seed phrase must stay offline.

questions.title: Backups
questions.prompt: What's the safest long-term backup strategy for your keys?

options.label: Screenshot the keys and store in iCloud/Google Photos
Paste keys in a notes app protected by FaceID
Follow the 3-2-1 rule (3 copies / 2 media / 1 offline)

questions.explanation: Use at least three copies across two media types with one offline (paper, metal). Cloud screenshots are single points of failure.

questions.title: New Client Test
questions.prompt: A brand-new Nostr app asks you to paste your private key to log in. What's the best move?

options.label: Paste the key if the app has more than 100 users
Use a signer / hardware key or wait until the client supports delegated signing
Generate a throwaway key and migrate later

questions.explanation: Never paste your main private key into new clients. Use a signer (NIP-46) or hardware solution and wait until delegated signing is supported.

questions.title: Metadata Hygiene
questions.prompt: How do you minimize metadata leaks on Nostr?

options.label: Leave location tags enabled—it helps discovery
Separate personas, strip EXIF data, avoid linking Lightning invoices between identities
Follow as many relays as possible with one profile

questions.explanation: Use separate profiles, disable location metadata, and keep Lightning/Zap info isolated when anonymity matters.

questions.title: Relay Strategy
questions.prompt: Which relay approach offers the best mix of reliability and privacy?

options.label: Use one mega-relay so everything is centralized
Use a small set of trusted paid relays + a rotating set for discovery
Only use free open relays and never curate

questions.explanation: Combining reputable paid relays with a few rotating public ones balances redundancy, spam resistance, and privacy.

questions.title: Zap Safety
questions.prompt: You're setting up zaps for the first time. Which step keeps your funds safest?

options.label: Reuse the same custodial wallet for every identity
Link a Lightning wallet you control and confirm zap requests before signing
Send your seed phrase to a relay so it can auto-withdraw

questions.explanation: Connect a wallet you control, confirm each request, and avoid sharing custodial accounts between identities.

quickstart.title: Quickstart
quickstart.description: Get up and running with Nostr in minutes with this hands-on quickstart guide.

questions.title: Getting Started
questions.prompt: What's the very first thing you need to use Nostr?

options.label: A credit card to pay for an account
A client app and a key pair

questions.explanation: To use Nostr, you need a client app (like Amethyst, Damus, or Iris) and a key pair (npub/nsec). No registration, payment, or approval required.

questions.title: Key Creation
questions.prompt: When you first open a Nostr client, what should you do with your keys?

options.label: Share them on Twitter for backup
Save them securely offline before doing anything else

questions.explanation: Immediately backup your keys offline (written down, encrypted file, or secure password manager) before you start posting. Losing your keys means losing your identity.

questions.title: Building Your Network
questions.prompt: How can you find people to follow when you're new to Nostr?

options.label: Import Twitter follows, use hashtags, or browse popular relays
Wait for the algorithm to suggest friends

questions.explanation: Many clients let you import Twitter followers who've also joined Nostr. You can also search hashtags, browse public feeds, or ask for recommendations.

questions.title: Client Selection
questions.prompt: Which Nostr client should you use?

options.label: Any client that works on your device and feels comfortable
The one with the most downloads

questions.explanation: There's no 'official' client. Choose one that works on your platform (iOS: Damus, Android: Amethyst, Web: Iris/Snort). Your identity works across all of them.

questions.title: Post Visibility
questions.prompt: Who can see your posts on Nostr?

options.label: Anyone using a relay that stores your posts

questions.explanation: Posts are public by default and visible to anyone using relays that store them. Think of it like a public bulletin board - anyone passing by can read it.

questions.title: Initial Relay Setup
questions.prompt: When starting out, how many relays should you connect to?
questions.explanation: Start with 3-5 well-known, reliable relays. This gives you good coverage without overwhelming your client. You can always add more later as you learn.

findingCommunity.title: Finding Community
findingCommunity.description: Discover how to find and join communities on Nostr.

questions.title: Sharing Identity
questions.prompt: How do you share your Nostr profile with someone?

options.label: They need to search your real name

questions.explanation: Your npub (public key starting with 'npub1...') is how people find and follow you. Share it like you would a username.

questions.title: Finding Groups
questions.prompt: What's the best way to find communities on Nostr?
questions.explanation: Communities form around hashtags and topics. Search for hashtags that interest you, follow active posters, and engage in conversations to discover your tribe.

questions.title: Twitter Migration
questions.prompt: Can you find your Twitter friends on Nostr?

options.label: Yes, many clients let you import Twitter followers who have Nostr accounts
Only if you pay for a premium feature

questions.explanation: Many Nostr clients offer Twitter import features. They check which of your Twitter follows have linked their Nostr npubs and let you follow them instantly.

questions.title: Direct Messaging
questions.prompt: What's proper etiquette when DMing someone new on Nostr?

options.label: Introduce yourself briefly and have a reason for reaching out

questions.explanation: Like any social platform, be respectful. Introduce yourself, explain why you're reaching out, and avoid unsolicited spam or promotions.

questions.title: Content Control
questions.prompt: How do you deal with unwanted content or users on Nostr?

options.label: Mute or block them - the choice is yours

questions.explanation: Nostr clients provide mute and block features. Since there's no central authority, YOU control what you see. Block spammers, mute topics, curate your experience.

questions.title: Creating Community
questions.prompt: How can you start your own community on Nostr?

options.label: Create a hashtag, share good content, and engage consistently

questions.explanation: Communities emerge organically around topics. Create a unique hashtag, post quality content regularly, reply to others, and be patient. Communities grow through engagement.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.description: Frequently asked questions about Nostr, answered in plain English.

questions.title: Company Ownership
questions.prompt: Who owns Nostr?

options.label: No one - it's an open protocol

questions.explanation: Nostr is an open protocol, not a company. Anyone can build on it. Jack Dorsey donated to its development but doesn't control it.

questions.title: Account Management
questions.prompt: Can you delete your Nostr account?

options.label: Yes, by clicking 'Delete Account' in settings
No, posts are distributed across relays and can't be fully erased

questions.explanation: Nostr posts are distributed to multiple relays. Once posted, you can't guarantee deletion because relays you don't control may keep copies. Post carefully.

questions.title: Mobile Access
questions.prompt: Can you use Nostr on mobile?

options.label: Yes, there are apps for both iOS and Android

questions.explanation: Nostr has native apps for both platforms: Damus (iOS), Amethyst (Android), and web clients work on mobile browsers too.

questions.title: Usage Cost
questions.prompt: Does it cost money to use Nostr?

options.label: No, the protocol is free (though some paid relays exist)
Only if you post more than 100 times

questions.explanation: Nostr is free to use. Many public relays are free. Some paid relays offer better performance or features, but they're optional.

questions.title: Moderation
questions.prompt: Who moderates content on Nostr?

options.label: Each relay operator sets their own rules, and users control their own experience

questions.explanation: There's no central moderation. Relay operators decide what to host on their servers. Users choose which relays to use and can mute/block content they don't want to see.

questions.title: Key Recovery
questions.prompt: What happens if you lose your private key?

options.label: Contact Nostr support to reset it
Your identity is lost forever - create a new key pair
Use your email to recover it

questions.explanation: There's no 'forgot password' option. If you lose your private key, you lose access to that identity permanently. This is why secure backups are critical.

relaysDemystified.title: Relays Demystified
relaysDemystified.description: Deep dive into how relays work with simple analogies and interactive tools.

questions.title: What is a Relay?
questions.prompt: What is a Nostr relay?

options.label: A device that boosts your WiFi signal
A server that stores and forwards Nostr messages

questions.explanation: Relays are servers that receive, store, and broadcast Nostr events (posts, likes, follows). They act as the infrastructure layer of the network.

questions.title: User Control
questions.prompt: Who decides which relays to use?

options.label: You choose which relays to connect to

questions.explanation: You have complete control over which relays you use. You can add, remove, or switch relays anytime in your client settings.

questions.title: Relay Types
questions.prompt: What's the difference between paid and free relays?

options.label: Paid relays have better performance and less spam

questions.explanation: Paid relays often offer better uptime, faster syncing, and less spam because they have resources to maintain quality and can ban abusive users.

questions.title: Data Storage
questions.prompt: How long do relays keep your posts?

options.label: It varies by relay - some keep forever, some delete old posts

questions.explanation: Each relay sets its own storage policies. Some archive everything indefinitely, others delete posts after a certain time or size limit. Use multiple relays for redundancy.

questions.title: Optimal Setup
questions.prompt: How many relays should you typically connect to?
questions.explanation: Most users find 3-10 relays provides good coverage without overwhelming their client. Too few = single points of failure. Too many = slower performance.

questions.title: Censorship
questions.prompt: Can a relay ban you?

options.label: Yes, a relay operator can refuse to store your posts, but you can use other relays
Only if you break federal law

questions.explanation: Individual relays can ban users or content. However, Nostr's decentralization means you can simply use different relays. Your identity isn't tied to any specific relay.

nip05Identity.title: NIP-05 Identity
nip05Identity.description: Set up your NIP-05 identifier and get a human-readable name like you@domain.com.

questions.title: NIP-05 Purpose
questions.prompt: What does NIP-05 provide?

options.label: A human-readable identifier (like you@domain.com) linked to your npub

questions.explanation: NIP-05 maps an email-style identifier (you@domain.com) to your npub, making it easier for people to find and verify you.

questions.title: Verification
questions.prompt: How is NIP-05 verified?

options.label: By uploading your ID to a central server
By placing a JSON file on a web server you control

questions.explanation: NIP-05 works by hosting a .well-known/nostr.json file on your domain that maps your identifier to your public key, proving you control that domain.

questions.title: Benefits
questions.prompt: What's a key benefit of having a NIP-05 identifier?

options.label: It hides your npub from everyone
It makes you easier to find and adds credibility

questions.explanation: NIP-05 makes your profile discoverable via an easy-to-remember name. It also provides verification (checkmark) showing you control that domain.

questions.title: Getting NIP-05
questions.prompt: How can you get a NIP-05 identifier?

options.label: Use a NIP-05 provider service or host it on your own domain

questions.explanation: You can either host NIP-05 on your own domain (requires a website) or use services like nostrplebs.com, nostr-check.com that provide identifiers.

questions.title: Security Consideration
questions.prompt: What should you know about NIP-05 and privacy?

options.label: It links your identity to a domain you control, which could deanonymize you
It makes your account completely anonymous

questions.explanation: NIP-05 ties your npub to a real domain, which may reveal your identity. If anonymity matters, consider whether linking to a personal domain is appropriate.

zapsAndLightning.title: Zaps & Lightning Network
zapsAndLightning.description: Master the art of sending and receiving Bitcoin payments (zaps) over the Lightning Network.

questions.title: Zap Definition
questions.prompt: What are 'zaps' on Nostr?

options.label: Bitcoin payments sent over the Lightning Network

questions.explanation: Zaps are Bitcoin micropayments sent via the Lightning Network. They allow you to tip or support content creators instantly with real money.

questions.title: Lightning Network
questions.prompt: How does the Lightning Network differ from regular Bitcoin?

options.label: It's faster and cheaper for small payments

questions.explanation: Lightning is a layer-2 payment protocol on top of Bitcoin. It enables instant, low-cost transactions perfect for micropayments like zaps.

questions.title: Wallet Setup
questions.prompt: What do you need to receive zaps?

options.label: A Lightning wallet connected to your Nostr profile

questions.explanation: To receive zaps, you need a Lightning wallet (custodial like Wallet of Satoshi, or self-custodial like Phoenix/BlueWallet) linked to your Nostr profile via a Lightning Address.

questions.title: Zap Privacy
questions.prompt: Are zaps private?

options.label: The amount and sender are visible on Lightning, but you can use different wallets for different identities

questions.explanation: Lightning payments are pseudonymous like Bitcoin. The transaction is visible but not tied to your identity unless you link wallets across personas. Use separate wallets for privacy.

questions.title: Wallet Types
questions.prompt: What's the difference between custodial and self-custodial Lightning wallets?

options.label: Custodial wallets hold your funds (easier), self-custodial means you control the keys (more secure)
Custodial wallets are only for Bitcoin, Lightning wallets are separate

questions.explanation: Custodial wallets (like Wallet of Satoshi) are user-friendly but the provider controls your funds. Self-custodial wallets (like Phoenix) give you full control but require more responsibility.

nostrTools.title: Essential Nostr Tools
nostrTools.description: A curated directory of the most useful Nostr tools and services for key management, media hosting, analytics, and more.

questions.title: Key Tools
questions.prompt: What can Nostr key converter tools do?

options.label: Convert between hex and bech32 (npub/nsec) formats

questions.explanation: Key converters translate between different key formats. For example, converting a hex public key to an npub format that starts with 'npub1...'.

questions.title: Media Storage
questions.prompt: How do you share images on Nostr?

options.label: Upload to Nostr's central image server
Use media hosting services (nostr.build, imgur) and paste the URL

questions.explanation: Nostr is text-based, so images are shared via URLs. Upload to media hosting services (nostr.build, void.cat) or IPFS, then include the link in your post.

questions.title: Analytics
questions.prompt: What can Nostr analytics tools show you?

options.label: Your follower growth, engagement stats, and reach

questions.explanation: Analytics tools analyze public Nostr data to show follower counts, engagement metrics, trending topics, and help you understand your reach on the network.

questions.title: Signer Apps
questions.prompt: What is a Nostr signer app?

options.label: An app that securely stores your private key and signs events for other apps

questions.explanation: Signers (like Amber, Nostrudel) securely hold your private key and sign events on behalf of other apps. This lets you use new clients without pasting your nsec everywhere.

questions.title: Backup Solutions
questions.prompt: What should you use for backing up your Nostr data?

options.label: Specialized backup tools that export your events to multiple relays
Trust that relays will keep everything forever

questions.explanation: Backup tools help export your posts and metadata, allowing you to restore your history or migrate to new relays. Don't rely on any single relay to keep your data forever.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.description: Common issues and how to fix them. From empty feeds to relay problems.

questions.title: Empty Feed
questions.prompt: Your feed is empty - what's the most likely cause?

options.label: You're not connected to any relays, or the relays have no content

questions.explanation: Empty feeds usually mean relay issues. Check that you're connected to active relays in your client settings. Try adding popular public relays.

questions.title: Post Visibility
questions.prompt: You posted something but your friends can't see it. Why?

options.label: You need to pay for premium posting
You and your friends are using different relays

questions.explanation: If you're using different relays than your friends, they won't see your posts. Share which relays you're using, or add relays in common.

questions.title: Connection Problems
questions.prompt: Your client keeps disconnecting from relays. What should you check?

options.label: Your internet connection and if the relay URLs are correct

questions.explanation: Check your internet connection first. Then verify relay URLs are correct (wss:// format). Some relays may be down temporarily - try different ones.

questions.title: Lost History
questions.prompt: Your old posts are missing. What happened?

options.label: The relay you posted to deleted old content
You need to upgrade to premium

questions.explanation: Relays have different storage policies. Some delete old posts to save space. Use multiple relays and backup tools to preserve your history.

questions.title: DM Issues
questions.prompt: Your direct messages aren't going through. What could be wrong?

options.label: You and the recipient don't share any common relays
You need to verify your phone number

questions.explanation: DMs require both users to be connected to relays that will store and forward the encrypted message. Make sure you share at least one relay with the recipient.

questions.title: Performance
questions.prompt: Your Nostr client is very slow. How can you improve it?

options.label: Connect to fewer, high-quality relays instead of many slow ones

questions.explanation: Too many relays or slow relays can bog down your client. Keep your relay list lean (3-10 fast, reliable relays) for best performance.

multiClient.title: Using Multiple Clients
multiClient.description: How to use multiple clients simultaneously and keep your data in sync.

questions.title: Identity Portability
questions.prompt: Can you use the same Nostr identity on multiple clients?

options.label: No, each client needs a different account
Yes, your keys work everywhere - import your nsec into any client

questions.explanation: Your identity is portable. Import your nsec into any Nostr client (Damus, Amethyst, Iris, etc.) and your profile, followers, and posts follow you.

questions.title: Data Synchronization
questions.prompt: How does data stay in sync across clients?

options.label: Via relays - all clients read from and write to the same relay network
You need to manually copy data between devices

questions.explanation: Relays act as the sync layer. When you post from one client, it goes to relays. Other clients read from those same relays to show your content.

questions.title: Client Features
questions.prompt: Why might you want to use different clients?

options.label: Different clients have different features, UIs, and device support
You're required to use at least 3 clients

questions.explanation: Clients are interfaces to the same network. Some excel on mobile, others have better desktop features. Use what works best for your current device or task.

questions.title: Security Across Clients
questions.prompt: How should you handle security when using multiple clients?

options.label: Use a signer app so you don't paste your nsec into every client
Email your nsec to yourself for easy access

questions.explanation: Use NIP-46 signers (like Amber) or browser extensions to avoid pasting your private key into multiple apps. This limits exposure if one client is compromised.

questions.title: Relay Configuration
questions.prompt: Should you use the same relays across all clients?

options.label: It's recommended for consistency, but not required
No, you must use different relays for each client

questions.explanation: Using similar relay configs across clients ensures consistent experience, but you can customize per client based on your needs for that device.

relayGuide.title: Relay Guide
relayGuide.description: Everything you need to know about choosing, connecting to, and managing relays.

questions.title: Selection Criteria
questions.prompt: What should you consider when choosing relays?

options.label: Reliability, speed, cost, and community overlap

questions.explanation: Good relay selection considers uptime (reliability), response speed, whether it's free or paid, and if people you want to interact with use it.

questions.title: Finding Relays
questions.prompt: How can you discover good relays?

options.label: Check relay lists shared by trusted community members
Only use the first relay you find

questions.explanation: Find relay recommendations from community members, relay directory sites, or see which relays your friends use. Quality matters more than quantity.

questions.title: Paid Relays
questions.prompt: Why might you pay for a relay?

options.label: Better uptime, support, and reduced spam

questions.explanation: Paid relays often offer better performance, support, spam filtering, and longevity because they have resources to maintain quality infrastructure.

questions.title: Switching Relays
questions.prompt: What happens when you switch to a new relay?

options.label: You lose all your followers and posts
Your future posts go to the new relay, but old posts stay where they were

questions.explanation: New posts go to your current relays. Historical posts remain on relays where they were originally posted. Your identity and followers stay with you.

questions.title: Monitoring
questions.prompt: How can you tell if a relay is working well?

options.label: Check connection status in your client and monitor for timeouts

questions.explanation: Most clients show relay connection status. If a relay shows errors, timeouts, or your feed stops updating, consider switching to a more reliable one.

privacySecurity.title: Privacy & Security
privacySecurity.description: Advanced privacy and security practices for power users.

questions.title: Identity Separation
questions.prompt: Why use separate Nostr identities (personas)?

options.label: To compartmentalize different aspects of your life and reduce correlation

questions.explanation: Separate personas prevent linking your activities. Keep professional, personal, and anonymous identities isolated to maintain privacy boundaries.

questions.title: Image Metadata
questions.prompt: Why should you strip EXIF data from images before posting?

options.label: EXIF can contain GPS coordinates and device info that deanonymizes you

questions.explanation: Photos often contain EXIF metadata including GPS location, camera model, and timestamps. Strip this data to protect your physical location and identity.

questions.title: Hardware Security
questions.prompt: What's the benefit of hardware signing devices?

options.label: Private keys never leave the secure hardware, protecting against malware

questions.explanation: Hardware signers keep your private keys in a secure, isolated chip. Even if your computer is compromised, the keys can't be extracted.

questions.title: Correlation Risks
questions.prompt: How can someone link your Nostr identity to your real identity?

options.label: By analyzing patterns, metadata, linked accounts, and shared information
They can't - Nostr is fully anonymous

questions.explanation: Privacy requires operational security. Avoid sharing identifying details, reuse of usernames, linking to identifiable social accounts, or posting location data.

questions.title: Secure Backups
questions.prompt: What's the safest way to backup your Nostr keys?

options.label: Encrypted file stored offline, or written on paper/metal in a secure location
Send to a friend via WhatsApp
Store in Google Drive with public sharing

questions.explanation: Encrypt your keys with a strong password and store offline. Physical media (paper, steel plates) in secure locations provide excellent long-term storage.

questions.title: Client Verification
questions.prompt: How can you verify a Nostr client is safe to use?

options.label: Check if it's open source, has been audited, and has community trust
If it has more than 1000 downloads it's safe

questions.explanation: Prefer open-source clients that can be audited by security researchers. Check community feedback, development activity, and use signer apps when possible.

nip17PrivateMessages.title: NIP-17: Private Direct Messages
nip17PrivateMessages.description: Learn about NIP-17, the secure replacement for NIP-04, and how to migrate your private messaging in Nostr

questions.title: NIP-17 Purpose
questions.prompt: What is NIP-17?

options.label: An improved encryption standard for private messages replacing NIP-04

questions.explanation: NIP-17 is the updated standard for end-to-end encrypted direct messages on Nostr, replacing the older NIP-04 with better security.

questions.title: Security Improvements
questions.prompt: Why is NIP-17 better than NIP-04?

options.label: Uses sealed sender (hides sender from relays) and improved encryption

questions.explanation: NIP-17 uses sealed sender technology so relays can't see who sent the message, and implements improved cryptographic protocols for better security.

questions.title: Migration
questions.prompt: Do you need to migrate from NIP-04 to NIP-17?

options.label: Yes, use a client that supports NIP-17 for new messages

questions.explanation: Use NIP-17 capable clients for new private messages. Old NIP-04 messages remain as-is. Most modern clients now use NIP-17 by default.

questions.title: Sealed Sender
questions.prompt: What does 'sealed sender' mean in NIP-17?

options.label: Relays can't see who sent the message, only who can decrypt it

questions.explanation: Sealed sender hides the sender's identity from relays. The relay sees the encrypted message and knows who should receive it, but not who sent it.

questions.title: Compatibility
questions.prompt: How do you know if your client supports NIP-17?

options.label: Check the client's documentation or settings for NIP-17 support
It's indicated by a blue checkmark

questions.explanation: Check your client's feature list or documentation. Modern clients like Damus, Amethyst, and others have adopted NIP-17 for private messaging.

protocolComparison.title: Complete Protocol Comparison
protocolComparison.description: A comprehensive technical comparison of the three major decentralized social protocols. Learn the architecture, trade-offs, and which protocol fits your needs.

questions.title: Nostr Design
questions.prompt: What's Nostr's core architectural philosophy?

options.label: Simple, dumb relays with smart clients - no central authority

questions.explanation: Nostr uses simple relays that just store and forward. Clients do the heavy lifting. No blockchain, no central servers, no admin hierarchy.

questions.title: ActivityPub (Mastodon)
questions.prompt: How does ActivityPub (Mastodon) differ from Nostr?

options.label: ActivityPub uses federated servers with admins; Nostr uses relays without accounts

questions.explanation: ActivityPub is federated - you join a specific server with admins. Nostr uses relays - no accounts on servers, your keys work everywhere instantly.

questions.title: Bluesky/AT Protocol
questions.prompt: How does Bluesky (AT Protocol) compare to Nostr?

options.label: Bluesky uses a more complex architecture with Personal Data Servers; Nostr is simpler

questions.explanation: Bluesky's AT Protocol uses Personal Data Servers and a more complex architecture. Nostr is intentionally simpler with just relays and keys.

questions.title: Censorship Resistance
questions.prompt: Which protocol offers the strongest censorship resistance?

options.label: Nostr - no server accounts, easy relay switching, no central authority

questions.explanation: Nostr's design makes it most resistant to censorship: no server accounts to ban, easy to switch relays, no company or foundation controlling it.

questions.title: UX Trade-offs
questions.prompt: What trade-off does Nostr make for its decentralization?

options.label: Users must manage their own keys and relay selection (more responsibility)

questions.explanation: Nostr's decentralization puts more responsibility on users: key management, relay selection, and understanding the architecture. This is the trade-off for freedom.

outboxModel.title: Understanding the Outbox Model
outboxModel.description: Learn how Nostr ensures your posts reach everyone who follows you through smart relay discovery

questions.title: Outbox Purpose
questions.prompt: What problem does the outbox model solve?

options.label: It tells followers which relays to check for your posts
It encrypts your posts for privacy
It stores all your posts in one place

questions.explanation: The outbox model publishes your relay preferences (kind:10002) so followers know where to find your content.

questions.title: Event Kind
questions.prompt: What event kind is used for the relay list metadata?
questions.explanation: kind:10002 is the replaceable event that stores your relay list with read/write markers.

questions.title: Relay Markers
questions.prompt: What does the 'write' marker in your relay list indicate?

options.label: Relays where you publish your posts

questions.explanation: The 'write' marker indicates your outbox - relays where you typically publish. 'Read' indicates where you check for mentions.

questions.title: Best Practice
questions.prompt: How many relays should you have in your list?
questions.explanation: 2-4 relays is optimal. More relays drain battery and provide diminishing returns as content propagates naturally.

questions.title: Relay Migration
questions.prompt: If you stop using a relay and switch to a new one, what happens to your followers?

options.label: They automatically find you on the new relay
You need to message each follower individually

questions.explanation: When you update your relay list (kind:10002), followers automatically start checking your new relays. No manual reconnection needed!

lostKeys.title: Lost Keys - Prevention Focus
lostKeys.description: Unfortunately, lost keys cannot be recovered. However, we can help you prevent this in the future.
steps: Create a new key pair using the Key Generator
Immediately save your nsec in 3+ secure locations
Consider using a password manager (1Password, Bitwarden)
Write it down on paper and store in a safe place
Never rely on browser cache or single device storage
tips: There is no 'Forgot Password' in Nostr
Your keys are your identity - treat them like cash
Test your backup by restoring from it

newUserFeed.title: Welcome! Your Feed is Empty
newUserFeed.description: As a new user, your feed is empty because you need to follow people first.
steps: Go to the Empty Feed Fixer tool below
Select a starter pack of accounts to follow
Wait a few minutes for content to load
tips: Start with a starter pack for your interests
Follow at least 10-20 accounts to see content
Connect to multiple relays for better coverage

partialFeed.title: Missing Some Posts
partialFeed.description: Partial content usually means relay connectivity issues.
steps: Check which relays you are connected to
Add more relays (aim for 5-10 diverse relays)
Wait a few minutes for sync to complete
Check if the missing users use different relays
tips: Different users post to different relays
More relays = more content but slower loading
Some relays may filter certain content

checkRelays.title: Check Your Relay Connections
steps: Check if you have 3+ relays connected

relayIssue.title: Relay Connection Issue
relayIssue.description: Connected but no content suggests relay problems.
tips: Relays sometimes go offline for maintenance

offlineRelays.title: All Relays Offline
offlineRelays.description: This usually indicates a network or configuration issue.
steps: Try different relays from the Relay Explorer
Check if client is blocked by firewall
Restart the app and try again
tips: Make sure URLs start with wss:// not https://
Try using a VPN if on restricted network

stuckConnecting.title: Stuck on Connecting
stuckConnecting.description: The client is having trouble reaching relays.
steps: Force close and reopen the app
Clear app cache/data if on mobile

notPublishing.title: Posts Not Publishing
notPublishing.description: Your posts are failing to send.
steps: Check if you have write-enabled relays
Verify you have enough relays (at least 1)
Try posting again - it might be temporary
Check relay status - some require payment
Reduce post length and try again

slowLoading.title: Slow Loading
steps: Use the Relay Explorer to find fast relays

unstableConnection.title: Unstable Connection
steps: Use relays geographically closer to you
Check if on unstable WiFi/mobile data

zapNothing.title: Zap Button Does Nothing
zapNothing.description: Zap functionality may not be configured.
steps: Ensure you have a lightning wallet connected
Verify your wallet has NWC configured
Try a different client that supports zaps
Check if the recipient accepts zaps

securityTips.title: Security Tips

Test your backup by restoring from it before deleting originals

explanation.deliveryDesc: Someone only sees Alice's post if they read from at least one of the relays she published it to.
explanation.insightDesc: Relays never pass posts to each other. If Alice publishes only to Relay 1 and Carol only reads from Relay 2, Carol will never see Alice's posts.

quickstartSimulator.title: Quickstart Simulator
quickstartSimulator.description: Simulate your first steps on Nostr. Learn the basics through interactive examples.

keyGen.description: Every Nostr account is just a pair of keys — generate a practice pair to see what they look like.
keyGen.important: These practice keys only work here — they aren't real. With real keys, share your npub freely, but keep your nsec in a password manager or signer app and never paste it into a website or send it to anyone.

quickstartSimulator.simulationNote: This is a simulation for practice — install the real app when you're ready to join Nostr.

relayStep.description: Relays are the servers that store and pass along your posts — connect to a few so more people can see what you write.

postStep.title: Make Your First Post

postStep.tip: Your first post is a good place to introduce yourself — many people add #introductions so others can find them.

followStep.title: Follow People
followStep.description: Your feed stays empty until you follow people, so follow at least three to fill it up.

interactStep.description: Likes, reposts, and replies are how conversations grow on Nostr.
interactStep.instruction: Click the heart to like the post and finish this step.

zapStep.title: Receive a Zap
zapStep.description: Zaps are small Bitcoin payments people send to posts they enjoy.
zapStep.invitation: Someone liked your first post enough to send you a few sats.
zapStep.earnInfo: Sats are small amounts of real Bitcoin, sent straight to the Lightning wallet linked to your profile.

completion.title: First Day Complete!

protocolComparisonUI.title: Protocol Comparison
protocolComparisonUI.description: Compare Nostr with other decentralized social protocols like ActivityPub (Mastodon) and AT Protocol (Bluesky).

identity.title: Identity
identity.centralized: Your account is owned by the platform. They can delete or suspend you at any time.
identity.nostr: You own your identity through cryptographic keys. No one can delete your account.

data.title: Data
data.centralized: Your posts and data are stored on company servers. They can delete or modify your content.
data.nostr: Your data is distributed across many relays. You control where your content lives.

clients.title: Clients
clients.centralized: You're locked into one platform's app. Switching means losing your followers.
clients.nostr: Use any client you want. Your identity and followers follow you everywhere.

censorship.title: Censorship Resistance
censorship.centralized: Platforms decide what you can say. They can censor or shadowban you.
censorship.nostr: No central authority controls speech. You can always find relays that will carry your content.

postFlowSimulator.title: Post Flow Simulator
postFlowSimulator.description: See how a post travels from your device to other users through the Nostr network.

stepDescriptions.0: You create a post on your device and sign it with your private key.
stepDescriptions.1: Your post is published to Relay 1, which stores and validates it.
stepDescriptions.2: Your post is also published to Relay 2 (and any other relays you use).
stepDescriptions.3: Your followers receive the post from the relays they are connected to.
